BOLD responses
We analysed the association between BMI as a continuous variable and blood-oxygen-level dependent (BOLD) responses in our two contrasts of interest.

To determine if neuronal response was related to BMI, first-level contrast images were entered into one-sample t -tests and BOLD response was regressed across all participants in a whole-brain regression analysis.

To determine between-group differences (in placebo condition) and within-group differences (effects of GLP-1 receptor activation), these first-level contrast images were entered into second-level random-effects analyses using two-sample t -tests and paired-sample t -tests respectively.

To determine if neuronal response was related to BMI, first-level contrast images were entered into one-sample t -tests and BOLD response was regressed across all participants in a whole-brain regression analysis.

Only brain activations that survived family-wise error (p < 0.05) correction for multiple comparisons at the voxel level within the ROIs using a small volume correction, or across the entire brain for regions not of interest a priori , are reported.
